decisions.title: Standardization of the Resume Data Model
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: The system lacked a standardized format to store personal profiles and historical job experience. To enable a modular AI automation pipeline, we needed to establish how the underlying profile and job history would be structured.
drivers: Modularity: The ability for AI and system tools to surgically update sections without rewriting the entire document or multiple related documents.
Version Control: Storing data in a flat, predictable, and trackable syntax suitable for Git or database history tracking.
Scalability: Ensuring the data model can scale to support multiple profiles, job histories, complex relationships, and dynamic output formats (e.g., Markdown, LaTeX, JSON).

decision_outcome.selected_option: Normalized JSON Schema with Flat Arrays
decision_outcome.justification: A fully structured JSON schema segregates resume sections into isolated, unique-ID-driven objects. Moving away from manual sequential keys (e.g., custom indexed objects) to industry-standard flat string arrays for lists (like skills) avoids redundant data tracking, simplifies sorting logic, and reduces LLM token overhead during transformation steps.
implications: Simplifies downstream AI processing, as parser validation can easily target specific JSON nodes.
Requires validation logic on the API layer to enforce the standard schema ($schema compliance).
Eliminated the overhead of custom key re-indexing code when mutating list items.

alternatives_considered.option: Flat document string storage
alternatives_considered.reasoning: While simple, treating the resume as a single block of un-tokenized text or markdown prevents surgical updates, causes massive token bloat, and is highly prone to format drift during AI generations.

alternatives_considered.option: Numeric Key-Mapped Skill Objects
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Mapping skills to sequential string keys (e.g., '1': 'Enterprise Architecture') introduced redundant data structures and added complexity, as deleting or re-ordering elements would force manual index calculations.

decisions.title: Consolidation of Accomplishments into Job History Schema
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Accomplishments were originally isolated in a standalone 'locked-accomplishments.json' file. However, accomplishments are inherently tied to specific roles, companies, and professional time periods. Functioning similarly to job-specific skills. Keeping them decoupled created data fragmentation and structural parsing overhead.
drivers: Cohesion: Grouping accomplishments directly as attributes of the relevant career milestone/role.
Data Efficiency: Streamlining the AI workflow by passing a single consolidated file ('locked-job-history.json') instead of orchestrating multiple file reads.
Logical Integrity: Ensuring that when a career entry is manipulated, its achievements and key impacts automatically remain bound to it.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Job History Bound Schema Integration
decision_outcome.justification: Embedding accomplishments directly as a nested array attribute (such as 'accomplishments' or 'bullet_points') within the specific job object of 'locked-job-history.json' structurally mirrors the real-world relationship between a role and its corresponding impact metrics. This simplifies data transformation logic and makes schema validation highly intuitive.
implications: Simplifies downstream resume-rendering tasks (e.g., converting to LaTeX, PDF, or Markdown) as the template generator only needs to loop over a single role array.
Reduces token overhead and state orchestration complexity for AI agentic workflows.
Deprecates 'locked-accomplishments.json' entirely, streamlining the system directory structure.

alternatives_considered.option: Standalone Accomplishments File mapped via Foreign Keys
alternatives_considered.reasoning: While normalized in a database sense, using foreign keys (e.g., 'exp_001') to link standalone accomplishments in a separate file forces the AI engine to perform programmatic joins across JSON documents. This adds fragile data layers and increases parsing failure rates.

decisions.title: Establishment of Sandboxed AI Workspaces via Epics
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Unrestricted AI agent file access introduces a significant risk of accidental file corruption, structural layout overwrites, and chaotic workspace pollution. To prevent this, the AI must have strict structural guardrails regulating where it is allowed to write or modify files, mapped to highly structured logical groupings of work.
drivers: Logical Organization: Organizing output assets cleanly by target companies and job description use cases to prevent document clutter.
Workflow Isolation (Epics Concept): Mirroring project management standards (like Jira Epics) where a high-level target objective (the Epic) houses individual technical iterations (the tasks/files).
Write-Access Security Guardrail: Imposing strict directory limitations on the AI, making core configuration files immutable while allowing complete autonomy inside dedicated execution paths.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Singular Target Directory Path: `.ai/history/epics/{company_name}/{output_files}`
decision_outcome.justification: Restricting the AI's write authority exclusively to a singular target path structured around `{company_name}` enforces rigorous context boundary management. The concept of 'Epics' perfectly mirrors Agile design by logically grouping distinct resume iterations, LinkedIn message assets, and tailored cover letters under the parent company namespace. All root-level files outside of this folder are programmatically rendered read-only (immutable) to the AI agent during execution.
implications: Significantly reduces file-system pollution by guaranteeing a predictable, nested structure.
Enforces an architectural security model where the AI is physically sandboxed out of master JSON stores.
Enables easy cleanup, auditing, and diff tracking per application target directly through version control.

alternatives_considered.option: Flat global directory output
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Storing all adapted resumes and cover letters in a flat, shared directory leads to fast-moving asset pollution, risk of file name collisions, and massive cognitive load for the user when looking for specific application versions.

alternatives_considered.option: Decoupled output directories by asset type (e.g., '/resumes', '/messages')
alternatives_considered.reasoning: While clean by asset type, this model fractures context. If an architect is applying to a specific target, having their resume in one root folder and their cover letter in another breaks the cohesive 'Epic' context, requiring the AI to search multiple directories to reconstruct a single application state.

decisions.title: Isolation of Source-of-Truth Workflow Templates
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: To prevent generation drift, the AI agent requires a consistent, repeatable baseline configuration (templates) to seed its outputs. However, if templates are stored within the active execution sandbox, they run the risk of being overwritten or corrupted by write-authorized AI tasks.
drivers: Consistency: Providing a guaranteed, stable starting point for every new generation run.
Human Governance: Ensuring baseline structural layouts (LaTeX templates, Cover Letter layouts, JSON profiles) are maintained exclusively by the human user.

Extensibility: Allowing the system to scale and gain new capabilities (e.g., adding a new format like 'plain-text-resume.txt' or 'cold-email-draft.md') without modifying the backend execution code or directory schemas.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Dedicated Read-Only Templates Directory Outside the Sandbox
decision_outcome.justification: Storing all source-of-truth templates in a dedicated directory `.ai/templates/`) located strictly outside the sandboxed `.ai/history/epics/` working directory. The AI agent is granted read-only permissions to this folder. To run a workflow, the agent copies a static template file to the target Epic directory and adapts it. Updates to styling, schema, or prompts are handled manually by the human user editing the root templates.
implications: Enforces a clean separation between human configuration (immutable to AI) and AI output (mutable within the sandbox).
Keeps directories logically organized, as developers/users immediately know where master schemas reside.
Enables easy scalability; adding a new baseline layout is as simple as adding a file to the template folder, requiring minimal structural pipeline code modifications.

alternatives_considered.option: In-Sandbox Template Seeding
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Stashing baseline templates inside active Epic workspace folders increases file overhead and risks the AI modifying the master templates mid-run, ruining reproducibility for future execution runs.

alternatives_considered.option: Hardcoding Templates in Script Code
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Embedding markdown or LaTeX templates directly inside script structures destroys ease-of-use and flexibility. It forces the user to write code just to tweak a margin or add a profile field, restricting future modular expansion.

decisions.title: Centralization and Immutability of AI Guardrails
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: AI agents require explicit structural schemas and styling guardrails to prevent output hallucinations, syntax violations, or context drift. If these governing rules are scattered across the workspace, nested inside mutable working directories, or hardcoded into application configurations, they can easily be corrupted by write-authorized AI tasks or lost to environment drift.
drivers: Absolute Immutability: Placing the critical configuration files that rule the AI out of write-reach of the AI itself.

Model and Environment Agnosticism: Isolating syntax rules and formatting policies in non-proprietary schemas (JSON, Markdown) so they remain fully portable across different LLM integrations or developer setups.
Organizational Clarity: Maintaining a distinct separation of concerns between operational run histories (Epics), starter layouts (Templates), and governing execution guardrails.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Centralized Read-Only Guardrails Directory: `.ai/guardrails/`
decision_outcome.justification: All schema blueprints (JSON data structures) and behavioral/formatting policies (such as `locked-formatting-rules.md`) will reside in a dedicated, singular directory: `.ai/guardrails/`. This folder is treated as strictly read-only (immutable) to all AI processes. By anchoring guardrails outside active workspace paths, we eliminate any path to accidental policy modifications while providing a clear, localized folder for human operators to maintain, review, and version-control core constraints.
implications: Prevents local model generation drift by ensuring structural validation layers and Markdown rules are protected from unauthorized rewrites.
Keeps administrative policies highly structured, visible, and isolated from dynamic workflow artifacts.
Allows seamless development-environment transitions, since governance files are independent of localized platform logic.

alternatives_considered.option: Inlining constraints in master prompt definitions
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Hardcoding formatting constraints and JSON data validation structures directly inside prompt definitions leads to massive token bloat, repetitive configurations, and severe maintenance pain across multiple system runs.

alternatives_considered.option: Placing guardrails inside target Epic working directories
alternatives_considered.reasoning: If guardrails are bundled alongside dynamic outputs within active workspace directories, they fall directly within the AI's write sandbox. This raises the risk of self-modification or deletion during agentic write loops.

decisions.title: Epic Branch Workflow with PR-Gated Merge to Main via GitHub Actions
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Resume tailoring work currently produces epic-scoped artifacts under `.ai/history/epics/{company_name}/`, but there is no formal version-control workflow governing when those outputs are promoted to the canonical `main` branch. Without a controlled merge path, finalized resumes, engineering logs, and outreach assets risk being committed directly to `main` without human review, making it difficult to audit AI-generated changes, reject incomplete work, or extend the pipeline with downstream automation that depends on a known-good state.
drivers: Human-in-the-Loop Governance: Require explicit human approval before any epic's generated artifacts become part of the canonical repository history on `main`.
Epic Isolation: Align Git branching with the existing Epic sandbox model (ADR-003) so each target company/application is developed on a dedicated feature branch until finalized.
Auditability: Preserve a reviewable PR diff that captures the full set of AI-generated outputs (engineering log, tailored resume, outreach) for a single application target.
Workflow Control: Gate promotion to `main` on both resume finalization and PR approval, establishing a deliberate release boundary rather than ad-hoc commits.
Extensibility: Create a merge-event hook on `main` that future GitHub Actions workflows can build on (e.g., notifications, artifact indexing, deployment, or integration triggers).

decision_outcome.selected_option: One Feature Branch per Epic (`feature/{company-name}-{position-name}`) with PR-Required Merge to Main via GitHub Actions
decision_outcome.justification: Each new application Epic begins on a dedicated feature branch named `feature/{company-name}-{position-name}` in kebab-case (e.g., `feature/volkswagen-group-solution-architect`), scoped to `.ai/history/epics/{company_name}/`. The Git branch name and Epic directory name are related but not identical: the Epic sandbox directory retains the human-readable company name per ADR-003 (e.g., `Volkswagen Group/`), while the branch slug applies kebab-case normalization to both the company and position derived from the job description. The user manually creates the feature branch before creating `job-description.md`. All AI tailoring iterations occur on that branch. PR readiness is governed by `.cursor/skills/resume-tailer/SKILL.md`: once the resume tailor workflow completes successfully (Steps 1–5), the agent commits epic artifacts, pushes to `origin`, and opens a pull request targeting `main`. Merge is permitted only after human PR approval. GitHub Actions runs initial validation checks on the PR (required artifact presence and parsed role-header chronology integrity); upon approved merge, `main` receives a clean, auditable snapshot of the completed Epic. Post-merge automation is explicitly deferred for the initial implementation.
implications: Branch-to-directory mapping: Git branch `feature/{company-name}-{position-name}` (kebab-case) maps one-to-one to Epic workspace `.ai/history/epics/{Company Name}/` (human-readable, ADR-003). Example: branch `feature/volkswagen-group-solution-architect` ↔ directory `.ai/history/epics/Volkswagen Group/`. The `{company-name}` slug is the kebab-case form of the Epic folder name; `{position-name}` is the kebab-case form of the target role title extracted from `job-description.md`.
Branch creation is handled manually by the user before `job-description.md` is created. The resume tailor workflow validates branch alignment at pre-flight; the agent does not create branches.

PR creation is automated as Step 5 of the resume tailor skill workflow (`.cursor/skills/resume-tailer/SKILL.md`): after Steps 1–4 produce all required artifacts, the agent commits, pushes to `origin`, and opens a pull request targeting `main`. Incomplete Epics never reach `main`.

Initial GitHub Actions CI checks (v1): (1) verify required Epic output files exist for merge (`engineering-log.md`, `tailored-resume.md`, `tailored-outreach.md`, `job-description.md`), and (2) parse `##` role section headers from `tailored-resume.md` and compare them in order against the corresponding headers in `.ai/templates/resume-master.md` — flagging any added, removed, reordered, or renamed roles (including date segments if present in headers). A failure on this check blocks merge.
Post-merge automation is out of scope for v1; the merge event hook on `main` is reserved for future ADR-defined extensions.
Incomplete or in-progress Epic work remains isolated from `main` until explicitly reviewed and approved.
PR diffs become the authoritative audit record for human review of AI-generated resume tailoring outputs.
Branch protection on `main` (required reviews, required status checks) becomes a prerequisite configuration in the GitHub repository.
Developers and AI agents must operate on Epic feature branches during active tailoring; direct writes to `main` for Epic artifacts are disallowed.

Review notification (v1): GitHub Actions workflow on `pull_request` opened/ready_for_review assigns the repository owner as reviewer, applies a `ready-for-review` label, and relies on native GitHub review-request notifications (email and/or mobile). External channels (Slack, Teams) deferred until needed.

alternatives_considered.option: Direct commit of Epic outputs to main
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Committing AI-generated resume artifacts directly to `main` bypasses human review, conflates in-progress and finalized work, and provides no structured audit boundary for rejecting or revising incomplete outputs.

alternatives_considered.option: Epic directories on main with local-only drafts
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Keeping all Epic folders on `main` and treating drafts as uncommitted local files fractures version history, loses team-visible progress tracking, and prevents PR-based review of the full artifact set before promotion.

alternatives_considered.option: Single long-lived integration branch for all Epics
alternatives_considered.reasoning: A shared integration branch mixes unrelated application targets, produces noisy diffs, and makes it impossible to approve or reject one Epic independently of another.

alternatives_considered.option: Manual merge without GitHub Actions or branch protection
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Relying solely on informal merge discipline lacks enforceable gates, provides no automated validation hook, and does not establish the CI/CD foundation needed for future pipeline extensions.

decisions.title: Job Search Discovery Sandbox and Multi-Skill Layout
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: The repository can tailor resumes for known job descriptions but has no governed discovery path for scanning approved ATS sources, normalizing listings, or reviewing matches without polluting epic sandboxes or violating aggregator TOS via scraping.
drivers: Sandbox Isolation: Keep discovery outputs separate from epic resume-tailor workspaces.
TOS Safety: Prefer public ATS Job Board APIs over LinkedIn/Indeed scraping.
Multi-Skill Layout: Orchestrator skill plus per-platform skills and tooling.
Human Governance: Skills under .cursor/skills remain human-maintained; agents do not mutate them during normal runs.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Platform-scoped sandbox under .ai/history/job-search/<platform>/ with orchestrator skill at .cursor/skills/job-search/SKILL.md
decision_outcome.justification: Discovery artifacts live under `.ai/history/job-search/<platform>/` with colocated platform skills and Python tooling. PowerShell wraps commands; Python implements fetch/normalize. Public ATS APIs only (Greenhouse Job Board API for POC). Local dashboard is read-only POC; promotion to resume-tailor is deferred.
implications: Extend core-architecture directory map with `.ai/history/job-search/`.
Do not treat `.ai/history/job-search/` as an epic sandbox; do not auto-trigger resume-tailer.
Orchestrator skills under `.cursor/skills/` are human-maintained and remain agent-immutable during normal job-search runs.
Job-search agent write access is limited to `.ai/history/job-search/`.

alternatives_considered.option: Store discovery pulls inside epic directories
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Epics are application-scoped; discovery is multi-company and would blur ADR-003 isolation.

alternatives_considered.option: Scrape LinkedIn/Indeed aggregators
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Violates TOS and is fragile; public ATS board APIs are the source of truth.

decisions.title: Standardization of the Job Search Data Model
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Incoming job listings from Greenhouse and future platforms must normalize to one structure. Without a locked guardrail schema, platform adapters can drift and documentation can be mistaken for the runtime contract.
drivers: Single Structure: All sources emit the same job object shape.
Guardrail Immutability: Align with ADR-005 for agent-read-only schemas.
Docs vs SoT Split: Mirror resume-schema.json vs resume-data-model.json.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Locked JSON Schema at .ai/guardrails/locked-job-search-data-model.json with docs-only companion at .ai/history/architectural-decisions/job-data-model.json
decision_outcome.justification: `.ai/guardrails/locked-job-search-data-model.json` is the architectural source of truth. All incoming jobs must match it after normalization. `.ai/history/architectural-decisions/job-data-model.json` is human-readable documentation only and must not be used for conformance. If docs and locked schema disagree, locked schema wins.
implications: fetch_jobs.py / normalize.py treat the locked file as the contract for emitted jobs.json.
Dashboard and future validators consume field names and status enum from the locked file.
Schema changes update the locked guardrail first, then sync the documentation companion.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat architectural-decisions/job-data-model.json as source of truth
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Documentation models are not suitable for programmatic validation; guardrails are the established SoT pattern (ADR-001/ADR-005).

alternatives_considered.option: Per-platform job schemas
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Breaks cross-platform dashboard aggregation and increases adapter drift.

decisions.title: Centralization of Locked Job Search Criteria
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Job discovery filters (titles, locations, exclusions) must be identical across Greenhouse and future platforms. Scattering criteria under per-platform folders or under `.ai/history/job-search/` risks drift, duplicate edits, and accidental agent mutation during pulls.
drivers: Single Source of Truth: One criteria file for all pullers.
Guardrail Immutability: Human-maintained, agent read-only (ADR-005).
Platform Separation: Platform folders hold only ATS-specific config such as boards.json.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Locked criteria file at .ai/guardrails/locked-job-search-criteria.json
decision_outcome.justification: Cross-platform filter criteria live in `.ai/guardrails/locked-job-search-criteria.json`. Every platform puller reads this file for title/location/remote/keyword matching. No per-platform search-criteria.json under `.ai/history/job-search/`.
implications: Preflight fails if locked-job-search-criteria.json is missing.
Criteria changes are intentional human edits, not agent side effects.
Core-architecture lists the new locked file alongside locked-profile.json and locked-job-history.json.

alternatives_considered.option: Per-platform search-criteria.json under job-search history
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Duplicates criteria and allows platforms to diverge silently.

alternatives_considered.option: Hardcode filters in Python scripts
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Forces code changes for routine title/location updates and hides policy from operators.

decisions.title: Rename Epics Sandbox and Templates into Resume-Tailor / Guardrails Naming
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: The resume application sandbox lived under `.ai/history/epics/` and the skill folder was named `resume-tailer`, while discovery already uses `.ai/history/job-search/`. Source ingestion templates lived under a separate `.ai/templates/` tree without the `locked-*` naming used elsewhere in guardrails. Divergent names and paths made agent instructions, CI paths, and operator docs harder to keep consistent and obscured the skill-to-sandbox relationship.
drivers: Sandbox Naming Alignment: Align the resume sandbox and skill with the `job-search` convention (`resume-tailor`).
Guardrail Consolidation: Place source ingestion templates under `.ai/guardrails/` using `locked-*-template` naming.

Git History Preservation: Perform structural path changes via `git mv` / Git rename detection so blame and `git log --follow` remain continuous for sandbox artifacts, templates, skill, and CI scripts (no recreate-and-delete).
Historical Integrity: Leave prior ADR bodies, plans, and existing sandbox output path strings unchanged; document former names in core-architecture for operators and agents.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Rename sandbox/skill to resume-tailor; move templates into guardrails as locked-*-template via git mv; update live runtime references
decision_outcome.justification: Renaming `.ai/history/epics/` to `.ai/history/resume-tailor/` and `.cursor/skills/resume-tailer/` to `.cursor/skills/resume-tailor/` aligns agent sandbox naming with job-search. Consolidating `.ai/templates/*` into `.ai/guardrails/locked-*-template.md` (including `locked-resume-master-template.md`) matches the locked guardrail pattern. All structural renames are executed with `git mv` so Git history remains continuous. Live skills, rules, CI scripts, workflows, and README are updated to the new paths; historical ADR/plan text is not rewritten. `core-architecture.mdc` records that the sandbox was previously `epics` and templates previously lived under `.ai/templates/`.
implications: Agents and CI use `.ai/history/resume-tailor/` and `.ai/guardrails/locked-resume-master-template.md` going forward.
CI script names, dist artifact paths, and manifest keys use resume-tailor terminology (`validate_resume_tailor_artifacts.py`, `dist/resume-tailor/`, `resume-tailor-manifest.json`).
Prior epic/template history remains reachable via `git log --follow` on the new paths.
Historical ADR-003/004/006 text and older plans may still say epics/templates; core-architecture naming note bridges that gap.
Nested company/position sandbox layout is deferred to a follow-on decision.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep epics as the concept name and only alias paths
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Leaves skill/sandbox naming inconsistent with job-search and continues dual vocabulary in live docs and CI.

alternatives_considered.option: Create new directories, copy content, delete old trees
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Breaks or obscures Git blame/history for sandbox artifacts, templates, skill, and CI scripts.

decisions.title: Nest Resume-Tailor Sandboxes as Company/Position
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Flat `.ai/history/resume-tailor/{company}/` sandboxes cannot hold multiple concurrent applications for the same company. Feature-branch slugs already encode both company and position (`feature/{company}-{position}`), while directories only encoded company, forcing ad-hoc naming and blocking parallel applications.
drivers: Multi-Application Support: Allow more than one open application per company without colliding sandboxes.
Branch/Path Alignment: Derive `feature/{company}-{position}` solely from the two kebab-case parent folders of `job-description.md`.
Git History Preservation: Migrate historical applications with `git mv` so renames remain continuous.
Legacy Isolation: Leave incomplete legacy test trees (e.g. Deloitte/) untouched until a later purge.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Nested kebab-case layout `.ai/history/resume-tailor/{company}/{position}/` with folder-derived branch identity
decision_outcome.justification: Nesting position under company mirrors the existing branch slug convention and makes sandbox identity path-authoritative. Historical complete applications are migrated via `git mv` to match known feature-branch slugs (e.g. `lts/integration-architect`, `volkswagen-group/solution-architect`). CI manifest and validation resolve sandboxes as two segments after `resume-tailor/` and ignore single-segment legacy dirs. Live skill, rules, and README globs/examples use the nested path; historical ADR-003/006 bodies and old plans are not rewritten.
implications: Agents and operators create sandboxes at `.ai/history/resume-tailor/{company}/{position}/job-description.md`.
Expected branch is always `feature/{company-folder}-{position-folder}` from folders, never JD free text.
CI `resume_tailor_dir_from_path` requires company + position segments; Deloitte flat layout is skipped.
Manifest `company_name` / `role_title` / `branch_slug` / `drive_folder` are filled from folder slugs.
Prior flat company paths remain reachable via `git log --follow` on nested destinations.

ADR-045 extends this layout; it does not replace it. Sandboxes remain two kebab-case segments after resume-tailor/. Queue-invoked position folders may include a source_job_id suffix. Manual runs and historical unsuffixed folders (e.g. capital-one/lead-data-engineer) stay valid and are not rewritten. CI still requires company + position segments; suffix is just more characters in the position segment.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep flat company directories
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Cannot support concurrent applications per company and leaves branch slugs encoding information the directory tree does not.

alternatives_considered.option: Derive branch identity from JD or engineering-log text
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Free-text titles drift from kebab folder/branch conventions (e.g. Sr Solutions Architect vs solution-architect) and break deterministic CI/agent checks.

decisions.title: Replace remote Boolean with Required work_location_type Enum
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: The job-search discovery model collapsed three work arrangements into a nullable boolean `remote`, so `false` meant onsite-or-hybrid and criteria filtering could not express include_hybrid vs include_onsite independently. Location include lists also mixed geography with arrangement tokens (Remote/Hybrid/On-Site), and scanning description_text for 'remote' produced false positives (e.g. LTS Technical Architect).
drivers: Arrangement Fidelity: Match the three-way intent already present in locked criteria (include_remote/hybrid/onsite).
Recall-First Filtering: Bare geography must not be forced to onsite when include_onsite is false.
Extraction Safety: Prefer structured location/office/metadata signals; never scan description_text for arrangement tokens.
Schema Uniformity: additionalProperties:false requires historical pulls to migrate so validation stays fail-closed without version branching.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Required work_location_type enum (remote|hybrid|onsite|unknown); criteria block renamed; schema 1.1; UTC Z timestamps
decision_outcome.justification: A single required enum replaces the boolean as the sole arrangement signal. Extraction precedence is allowlisted board metadata, then location.name + offices[].name; bare geography yields unknown. remote bypasses geography; unknown always passes the arrangement gate while include_* toggles apply only to known values. locations.include is reduced to pure geography. Envelope schema_version becomes 1.1; timestamps are UTC with Z. Historical 2026-08-06 and 2026-08-08 pulls are migrated in place.
implications: locked-job-search-data-model.json drops remote and requires work_location_type.
locked-job-search-criteria.json renames the remote block to work_location_type and bumps to 1.1.0.
Pull scripts live under .github/scripts/job-search/ with merge-append default and --rebuild overwrite (all rows new, today UTC only).
validate_jobs.py gates commits with Draft7 + FormatChecker and file-local semantic checks.
Scheduled workflow job-search-pull.yml commits validated pulls to main via github-actions[bot].

alternatives_considered.option: Keep remote boolean and add a separate work_mode field
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Two overlapping arrangement signals create ambiguity and force awkward false=onsite-or-hybrid semantics.

alternatives_considered.option: Map bare geography to onsite
alternatives_considered.reasoning: With include_onsite:false, NJ/NY roles without an explicit remote/hybrid token would be dropped before Phase 1b analysis.

alternatives_considered.option: Scan description_text for arrangement keywords
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Produces false positives when requirements mention remote work experience without the role being remote.

decisions.title: Scheduled Greenhouse Pull via GitHub Actions Direct-to-Main
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Greenhouse discovery originally ran only from a local Cursor skill / pull-jobs.ps1 entrypoint, so pulls stopped when the workstation was offline. Phase 1 needed a scheduled, non-LLM pull path that validates against the locked data model and persists results without a human PR gate, while leaving resume-tailor PR review (ADR-006) unchanged.
drivers: Offline Continuity: Daily discovery must continue without a local agent session.
Fail-Closed Persistence: Invalid jobs.json must never land on main.
Cost Control: Short ubuntu-latest jobs, no sleep retries, GITHUB_TOKEN so data commits do not re-trigger CD Main.
Layout: GHA automation under .github/; sandbox data under .ai/history/job-search/.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Cron + workflow_dispatch Job Search Pull workflow committing validated merge/rebuild artifacts to main
decision_outcome.justification: Smoke-confirmed on 2026-08-11: happy-path merge committed greenhouse/src/2026-08-11/jobs.json; rebuild reset that day to status=new leaving prior dates untouched; past-date and non-main dispatch failed before write; overlapping dispatches serialized via concurrency group cancel-in-progress:false; bot commits used github-actions[bot] and did not trigger CD Main. Scripts live at .github/scripts/job-search/ with merge-append default, --rebuild today-only overwrite, and validate_jobs.py gating the commit step.
implications: Primary operator path is gh workflow run job-search-pull.yml on main; pull-jobs.ps1 remains a local wrapper.
Pull owns new/active statuses only; analysis and handoff remain Phase 1b/2.

Architecture ADR records shipped behavior after smoke; data-model change remains ADR-012.

alternatives_considered.reasoning: Free-tier branch protection cannot enforce required PRs; Option A with GITHUB_TOKEN is viable and avoids per-day PR noise.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep discovery only in the local Cursor job-search skill
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Does not meet offline continuity; LLM session cost is wasted on non-LLM HTTP pulls.

decisions.title: Locked Word Resume Template Guardrail
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

implications: Normal resume-tailor runs never write .ai/guardrails/.
CI requires the sandbox .docx with no leftover {{ placeholders.
CD stages and uploads the sandbox application .docx.

alternatives_considered.reasoning: Leaves contact/education as copy-paste identity and keeps CD off the application document.

alternatives_considered.reasoning: PDF conversion is out of scope. The application artifact is .docx.

alternatives_considered.reasoning: Those fields belong on locked-professional-summary.json (ADR-019). Criteria stay puller filters.

decisions.title: Locked Contact Guardrail
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Contact and education in the hand-edited Word resume are copy-paste identity, not guardrail data. resume-schema.json nested contact inside a composed resume instance and was unused at runtime. fill_resume.py needs a parent identity object that holds foreign keys to each resume section without embedding those children.
drivers: One Section, One Locked File: Contact identity lives in its own guardrail matching the resume-data-model.json contact object.
Parent Holds FKs: education_id, skills_id, job_history_id, and professional_summary_id resolve to child ids; children are not nested in contact.
Guardrail Immutability: Align with ADR-005; agents read locked-contact.json and do not write it during a normal resume-tailor run.

decision_outcome.selected_option: locked-contact.json instance of the data-model contact object (identity plus four child FKs, no nested children)
decision_outcome.justification: A standalone contact guardrail is the parent of education, skills, job history, and professional summary. Sample payload is John / Doe / john.doe@example.com / 555-555-5555 / New York / NY / 10001 / US. links may be []. All FKs must resolve. resume-data-model.json documents the join contract; resume-schema.json is deleted.

Word header identity ({{CONTACT_*}}) comes from this file, not from the layout sample .docx.
CI syntax-checks locked-contact.json. Historical ADR-008 text that mentions resume-schema.json is not rewritten.

alternatives_considered.option: Embed education, skills, job history, and professional summary inside contact
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Collapses independent section files and forces fill_resume.py to parse nested blobs instead of ID joins.

alternatives_considered.option: Hardcode contact in locked-resume-template.docx
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Leaves identity as layout rather than guardrail data and cannot validate FKs.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep resume-schema.json as the contact contract
alternatives_considered.reasoning: The schema was unused at runtime (CI JSON-parse only) and modeled a nested John Doe instance, not the join contract.

decisions.title: Locked Education Guardrail

Does Not Implement Phase 1b: Does not extend ADR-014. Does not reuse qualifications.education.

implications: CI syntax-checks locked-education.json.
Word education lines come from this file, not from the layout sample .docx.
Phase 1b / ADR-014 / qualifications remain out of scope.

alternatives_considered.option: Nest education on contact
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Breaks the one-section-one-file join contract and embeds a child blob in the parent.

alternatives_considered.option: Bake education into locked-resume-template.docx
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Leaves education as layout rather than guardrail data.

alternatives_considered.option: Reuse Phase 1b qualifications.education on the profile/skills file
alternatives_considered.reasoning: ADR-014 is reserved and not written. This build does not implement qualifications.

decisions.title: Rename Profile to Locked Skills
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: locked-profile.json is named as a catch-all profile but is consumed as a skill vocabulary. It has no join key to contact. target_focus and summary on the same file are a distinct resume section, not skills.
drivers: Accurate Naming: The file is a skill vocabulary (selected_skills / all_skills), not a profile.
Git History Preservation: Structural rename via git mv so blame and git log --follow remain continuous (ADR-010 pattern).
Parent Holds the FK: contact.skills_id joins to skills.id. Skills does not carry contact_id.
Flatten Wrapper: Drop the shipped numeric "1" wrapper so the object matches the resume-data-model.json skills section.

decision_outcome.selected_option: git mv .ai/guardrails/locked-profile.json to .ai/guardrails/locked-skills.json; flatten wrapper; keep selected_skills/all_skills; contact.skills_id -> skills.id
decision_outcome.justification: Renaming to locked-skills.json matches how resume-tailor actually consumes the file. Flattening the "1" wrapper and adding id skl_001 makes the object joinable. target_focus and summary leave this file under ADR-019. Live consumers are updated; historical ADR/plan/sandbox text is not rewritten.
implications: Live skill, CI, and README path references to locked-profile.json are updated to locked-skills.json.
selected_skills and all_skills lists are unchanged.
fill_resume.py reads locked-skills.json for {{SKILL_NN}}; it does not read a profile file.
Historical ADR/plan/sandbox text that still says locked-profile.json stays as-is.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the profile name
alternatives_considered.reasoning: The name implies a catch-all identity/summary object and continues to mislead operators and agents.

alternatives_considered.option: Nest skills inside contact
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Breaks one-section-one-file and the contact-as-parent FK pattern.

alternatives_considered.option: Copy instead of git mv
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Breaks or obscures Git blame/history for the skill vocabulary (ADR-010).

decisions.title: Locked Professional Summary Guardrail
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: target_focus and summary lived on locked-profile.json (now locked-skills.json). They are a distinct resume section, not a skill vocabulary and not job-search filter criteria. Putting them on locked-job-search-criteria.json would force fill_resume.py to read a puller-filter file.
drivers: Section Isolation: Professional summary is its own locked object matching resume-data-model.json.
Exact String Copy: target_focus and summary are copied exactly from the former profile file; no rewrite.
Fill Isolation: fill_resume.py reads this file for {{SUMMARY}} / {{TARGET_FOCUS}}. It does not read locked-job-search-criteria.json.
Does Not Extend ADR-009: Job-search criteria stay titles/locations/arrangement/keywords.

decision_outcome.selected_option: New .ai/guardrails/locked-professional-summary.json matching the professional_summary object; contact.professional_summary_id -> professional_summary.id
decision_outcome.justification: A dedicated guardrail keeps positioning headline and summary off the skills file and off job-search criteria. Child of contact via professional_summary_id. Exact current strings from the former locked-profile.json.
implications: CI syntax-checks locked-professional-summary.json.
Resume-tailor preflight requires this file. Job-search criteria and fetch_jobs.py are unchanged.
The job-search agent is out of this ADR; it may later read this guardrail like any other.

alternatives_considered.option: Leave target_focus and summary on locked-skills.json
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Keeps a distinct resume section mixed into the skill vocabulary.

alternatives_considered.option: Put target_focus and summary on locked-job-search-criteria.json
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Would force fill_resume.py to read a puller-filter file and mix resume copy with discovery filters.

alternatives_considered.option: Embed summary fields in contact
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Breaks one-section-one-file; contact holds FKs only.

alternatives_considered.option: Duplicate the fields across resume and job-search files
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Creates drift between two sources of the same strings.

decisions.title: Job History Is a Child of Contact
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: locked-job-history.json had no identity key and no relationship to contact. The former docs model treated job_history as a nested sibling of contact. fill_resume.py cannot validate a join without an envelope id.
drivers: Join Contract: contact.job_history_id joins to job_history.id.
Preserve Role Keys: Digit-only keys "1"..."12" remain roles; ignore id when iterating positions.
Do Not Array-Convert: Numeric role keys stay an object map, not a JSON array.

decision_outcome.justification: An envelope id (jh_001) as a sibling of "1"..."12" makes job history a child of contact without rewriting role payloads. fill_resume.py aborts if contact.job_history_id does not match job_history.id.
implications: Role keys and payloads are unchanged.
Iterators skip the id key and treat digit-only keys as roles.
Fact conflicts still prefer locked-resume-master-template.md and locked-job-history.json over the layout sample .docx.

alternatives_considered.option: Nest jobs inside contact
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Breaks one-section-one-file and would duplicate the large role map into contact.

alternatives_considered.option: Put contact_id on every role
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Repeats the parent FK twelve times and still leaves the file without an envelope identity.

alternatives_considered.option: Convert "1"..."12" into a JSON array
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Would rewrite the locked chronology shape consumed by resume-tailor and CI.

decisions.title: Convention-Based Word Placeholder Binding
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: fill_resume.py hardcoded a per-field map of Word tokens ({{CONTACT_FIRST_NAME}}, {{EDU_*}}, {{SUMMARY}}, {{ROLE_N_*}}, {{SKILL_NN}}). Adding or renaming a placeholder in locked-resume-template.docx required a Python change.
drivers: Template Independence: The locked .docx can gain tokens such as {{CONTACT_COUNTRY}} or {{JOB_HISTORY_6_TITLE}} with no filler edit.
Object-Field Names: Token bodies follow join-contract keys: {{OBJECT_FIELD}}, {{OBJECT_INDEX_FIELD}}, {{OBJECT_ARRAYFIELD_INDEX_FIELD}} (1-based).
Overlay Isolation: {{SKILL_NN}} and {{JOB_HISTORY_N_BN}} come from sandbox tailored-resume.md, not locked-skills.json or role accomplishments.
No Aliases: {{ROLE_*}}, {{EDU_*}}, {{SUMMARY}}, and {{CONTACT_LINK_URL}} are unknown tokens and abort.

decision_outcome.selected_option: fill_resume.py discovers {{TOKENS}} in the template and resolves them by naming convention against join-contract objects; overlay tokens bind to tailored-resume.md; unknown object/field aborts; missing optional slots fill as empty string
decision_outcome.justification: A longest-object-prefix walk against resume-data-model.json section keys removes the hardcoded field map. JOB_HISTORY_5 is locked key "5". CONTACT_LINKS_1_URL is contact.links[0].url. Tailored bullets join by matching the ## title to job_history[key].title. derive_template.py emits the same names. The user renames tokens in locked-resume-template.docx; normal fills never write .ai/guardrails/.
implications: fill_resume.py deletes build_mapping() and first_contact_link_url().
Adding a scalar or indexed token to the locked .docx requires no Python change when the path exists on a loaded object.
Unknown tokens abort. Missing optional slots (no links[1], no SKILL_40, no tailored section for a referenced job_history key) become "" and empty paragraphs are removed.
When tailored-resume.md has no ## title matching job_history[key].title, that key's locked header fields are also left empty.
Historical ADR-015–020 text that still shows old token names is not rewritten.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep a hardcoded placeholder map in fill_resume.py
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Every template edit would require a matching Python change.

alternatives_considered.option: Bind JOB_HISTORY_5 to the fifth tailored ## block
alternatives_considered.reasoning: The index is the locked digit key "5", not display order.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep old-name aliases (ROLE_, EDU_, SUMMARY, CONTACT_LINK_URL)
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Aliases freeze the old map and hide template drift.

alternatives_considered.option: Agent rewrites locked-resume-template.docx
alternatives_considered.reasoning: .ai/guardrails/ stays user-owned for this cutover; derive_template.py only emits new names if the user runs it.

decisions.title: CI Close-Missing Jobs on Nearest Prior Pull File
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Scheduled Greenhouse pull only wrote status new or active. Listings that dropped off a board vanished from the new dated jobs.json and older dated files were never updated, so closed was unused. Phase 1b analysis must not invent closed locally.
drivers: CI Ownership: Closing missing ids is a pull/CI concern, not a local analysis-agent task.
Prior Snapshot: Today's file stays live listings only; closed rows are stamped on the nearest prior dated jobs.json.
Gap Days: Lookback is the existing 30-day nearest prior file, not calendar yesterday.
Fail-Closed: Both today's file and the patched prior file validate before commit.

decision_outcome.selected_option: After writing today's jobs.json, mark status=closed on nearest-prior rows whose id is absent from today; already-closed is a no-op
decision_outcome.justification: Reuse prior_job_ids' nearest prior file. Ids still present today are unchanged. Already closed rows are not rewritten. Same-day merge stays append-only. Rebuild still overwrites today as all new, then runs the same close-missing step. This supersedes ADR-013's implication that pull owns new/active only.
implications: fetch_jobs.py patches the nearest prior jobs.json and prints SUMMARY closed= and prior=.
job-search-pull.yml commits the prior date folder when it changed and validates both files.
locked-job-search-data-model.json is unchanged (closed already in the enum).
A job closed on day N-1 and absent on day N looks like new if it returns on day N+1 (nearest prior is day N). Phase 1b G5 may later restore approved/rejected/completed on reappearance.
Analysis agents must not invent closed.

alternatives_considered.option: Copy closed rows into today's jobs.json
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Today's file would mix live listings with closed history and would create analysis stubs for closed ids.

alternatives_considered.option: Let the analysis agent invent closed
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Closing is a pull/CI fact about board presence, not a qualification decision.

alternatives_considered.option: Close against calendar yesterday only
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Scheduled pulls may skip days; shipped lookback already uses the nearest prior file within 30 days.

decisions.title: Pull-Time Per-Job Analysis Sidecar Stubs
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Qualification analysis cannot live in a dated batch sidecar. Identity, revision history, and parallel agents require one analysis file per job, created when the daily jobs.json is committed, not when an agent first analyzes.
drivers: Windows-safe filenames: encode JOB.id by replacing : with -; suffix -analysis.json.
Stub identity: analysis_id 0 / revision 0 is a real unfilled row; first fill mutates in place to 1 / 1.
Create-if-not-exists on daily merge; --rebuild today deletes and recreates matching analysis files and drops matching approved-jobs.json rows.
One locked job-search schema: extend locked-job-search-data-model.json with ANALYSIS_FILE. No locked-analysis-schema.json.

decision_outcome.selected_option: write_analysis_stubs.py after fetch_jobs.py creates missing greenhouse/analyses stubs and a missing approved-jobs.json envelope; validators select $defs by path
decision_outcome.justification: Pull remains jobs-only in fetch_jobs.py. Stubs are schema-valid unfilled ANALYSIS_FILE documents. Analysis later fills the same file. ADR-014 is cancelled and must not be reused for this decision.
implications: jobs.json status enum is new|active|closed only. Qualification approved|rejected is sidecar decision.
approved-jobs.json rows require analysis_id as an FK when present. Pull never inserts rows.
CI validates changed analyses/*-analysis.json files as stub-shaped ANALYSIS_FILE documents.
Phase 1b analysis ADRs use numbers after 023.

alternatives_considered.option: Dated src/{YYYY-MM-DD}/job-analysis.json written by the analysis agent
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Batch files collide under parallel agents and lose per-job history across pull dates.

alternatives_considered.option: Reuse ADR-014 for pull-time stubs
alternatives_considered.reasoning: ADR-014 is cancelled. Candidate-evidence SoT is locked-job-data-model.json, a different decision.

decisions.title: Profile Qualifications Blob (Cancelled)
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Phase 1b originally reserved a profile-level qualifications blob and a profile-data-model.json companion. That grain conflicted with contact-parent ERD instances already used by resume fill.
drivers: Single analysis SoT: locked-job-data-model.json is the ERD schema.
No locked-profile.json recreation (ADR-018 renamed the former profile file to locked-skills.json).
Placeholder only: this number stays cancelled and is not reused.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Cancel ADR-014. Do not write profile-data-model.json. Candidate evidence lives on locked-job-data-model.json plus locked instance files.
decision_outcome.justification: Contact remains the parent object. Certifications, clearance, and licenses are related instance files with FKs on contact. A profile blob would duplicate that grain.
implications: ADR-016 education and later resume ADRs are not extended by this cancelled decision.
Live candidate-evidence ADR is ADR-024.
Do not reuse 014 for pull-time stubs (ADR-023) or analysis fill (ADR-025).

alternatives_considered.option: Implement the 2026-08-13 qualifications blob on locked-profile.json
alternatives_considered.reasoning: The profile file was renamed; qualifications are derived at analysis time from the ERD.

decisions.title: Candidate Evidence ERD as locked-job-data-model.json
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Qualification analysis needs a locked candidate evidence set (identity, education, skills, history, certifications, licenses, clearance, work authorization, mobility) without inventing a second profile schema or per-file schemas for credential children.
drivers: Single analysis JSON Schema: locked-job-data-model.json covers the ERD.
Instance files under .ai/guardrails/ stay the live values.
Missing field means not held; expired dated credentials are not currently held.
Requirement option A: prose evidence + note, no structured ERD pointers in sidecars.

decision_outcome.selected_option: locked-job-data-model.json is the analysis ERD schema. New instance files locked-certifications.json, locked-clearance.json, and locked-licenses.json. Contact work_authorization and mobility are string arrays with FKs certifications_id, clearance_id, licenses_id.
decision_outcome.justification: Keeps contact as parent, reuses shipped education/skills/history/summary, and avoids a cancelled profile blob. Analysis reads these files; resume fill does not require the new FKs until a later education-envelope change.
implications: G2 values: US Citizen + W-2; NY Metro Area, willing to relocate, < 25% travel; AWS Certified Solutions Architect 6/2022-6/2025; licenses and clearance envelopes with no digit rows.
Education remains the shipped B.S. singleton. High school stays dropped.
No contact_id on children until Phase 2 multi-contact.

alternatives_considered.option: Per-file JSON Schemas for certifications, clearance, and licenses
alternatives_considered.reasoning: G3 locked a single analysis schema. Sidecar, queue, and policy stay separate.

alternatives_considered.option: Revive ADR-014 / locked-profile.json
alternatives_considered.reasoning: ADR-014 is cancelled. Skills already occupy the former profile path.

decisions.title: Analysis Fill, Queue Files, and Joined Pipeline Status
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Pull-time stubs (ADR-023) are unfilled. Analysis must fill per-job sidecars, mint batch identity on queue files, and keep jobs.json presence-only. Dashboard overall status is a join, not a jobs.json write.
drivers: run_id minted only by generate-analysis-queue.py (uuid4 hex).
Queue invoke: fail-closed if queue/ is not empty; one incomplete file per job-analysis skill invoke.
First fill mutates stub 0/0 to 1/1 in place. From-scratch appends (G6) are a separate path.
Analysis never writes approved-jobs.json. Orchestrator consume is Phase 2.
G5 join: queue execution, else sidecar decision, else jobs.json new|active. Hide closed.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Queue files at .ai/history/job-search/queue/{run_id}-analysis-request.json with per-job status pending|analysis_complete. Skill fills sidecars then marks analysis_complete. Validators join sidecar job_id to any dated jobs.json and approved-jobs analysis_id to sidecar analyses[].
decision_outcome.justification: Separates pull stubs from analysis fill, keeps batch identity on the queue file and filled rows only, and leaves ledger upserts to Phase 2.
implications: Live queue files are gitignored; fixtures live under tests/fixtures/.
decision_impact is always none. Research sources are contextual only.
jobs.json validation does not require a sidecar. Sidecar validation does not require jobs.json.status to match decision.
analysis_runs[] telemetry is Phase 2. Phase 1b stores run_id only.

alternatives_considered.option: Analysis upserts approved-jobs.json on approved
alternatives_considered.reasoning: G10: analysis skill never writes the ledger in 1b. Orchestrator consume is Phase 2.

alternatives_considered.option: Mint run_id inside the analysis skill
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Generator is the single mint site so every job in a queue file shares one id.

decisions.title: Sequential Analysis Batches and Execution Cost Policy
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Qualification analysis is token-expensive. Unbounded parallelism and unbounded research would burn cost without a locked policy file.
drivers: Token minimization is the primary 1b driver.
Fresh agent per batch so durable JSON, not conversation context, carries progress.
Human-maintained locked-job-analysis-policy.json.
Phase 2 may add confirmation-gated bounded parallelism; unused knobs stay off disk in 1b.

decision_outcome.selected_option: locked-job-analysis-policy.json with default_mode sequential, max_jobs_per_agent 10, fresh_agent_per_batch true, and research max_web_searches_per_job / max_web_fetches_per_job unlimited. job-analysis skill processes one queue file per invoke.
decision_outcome.justification: Ten-job sequential batches bound context. Unlimited research matches resume-tailor parity for first-fill/from-scratch; 0/null skip a tool; omitted/negative halt. Parallel max_parallel_agents and confirmation keys wait for Phase 2.
implications: Phase 1b does not enable parallel analysis agents.
Phase 2 intent: Yes/No before at most two concurrent analysis agents; workers stay read-only; orchestrator applies edits serially.
Policy changes are human decisions. The skill never edits the policy file.

alternatives_considered.option: Write unused parallel knobs on disk in 1b
alternatives_considered.reasoning: G10 I3 overlay: only 1b-used execution keys plus research unlimited. ADR records Phase 2 intent without shipping dead knobs.

alternatives_considered.option: Nested Task agents drain every queue file in one invoke
alternatives_considered.reasoning: One file per invoke. Multi-file drain is the parent orchestrator in Phase 2.

decisions.title: 30-Day Dated Pull Retention Purge (Current Main Tree Only)
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Dated src/{YYYY-MM-DD}/ folders grow without bound on main. Pull lookback already uses a single nearest prior file within 30 days. Unbounded dated history is not required for merge status or close-wins once a folder is outside that window.
drivers: Match pull lookback window (N = 30 UTC calendar days).
Purge current main tree only; do not rewrite git history.
Keep sidecars, ledger, queue, dashboard, and lookback-window folders.

decision_outcome.selected_option: After analysis consume, delete .ai/history/job-search/{platform}/src/{YYYY-MM-DD}/ directories whose folder date is strictly older than UTC today minus 30 days. Include those deletions in the post-analysis job-search commit. git rm / tree delete only.
decision_outcome.justification: Thirty UTC days matches shipped pull lookback. Sidecar identity is job_id, not pull date. Ledger and queue stay durable.
implications: Closed rows that exist only on a purged dated jobs.json leave the live tree.
Generator/eligibility must tolerate a job last seen only on a purged day.
Actions stay source-scoped; orchestrator owns retention.

alternatives_considered.option: Purge analyses/ or approved-jobs.json with the dated folders
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Breaks G4 FKs and the resume-tailor ledger.

alternatives_considered.option: History rewrite (git filter-repo / force-push)
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Violates no-history-rewrite lock.

alternatives_considered.option: N not equal to 30
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Would diverge from shipped pull lookback and risk empty lookback after purge.

alternatives_considered.option: Purge during GHA pull
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Actions stay source-scoped; orchestrator owns retention.

decisions.title: Queue-Invoked Resume-Tailor May Create Feature Branches
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Manual resume-tailor requires the user to create feature/{company}-{position} before job-description.md. Queue-invoked Phase 2 fan-out cannot wait for that manual step, but the PR review/merge gate must stay.
drivers: Orchestrator is scripts + git only and does not create feature branches.
One feature branch maps to one sandbox path (ADR-011).
Slugs come from kebab_case(company) and kebab_case(title) on the queue row, not JD free text.

decision_outcome.selected_option: When invoked from a Phase 2 resume-tailor queue row, the resume-tailor skill may run git checkout -b feature/{company_slug}-{position_slug} from current main. PR review/merge gate unchanged. Orchestrator does not create feature branches.
decision_outcome.justification: Keeps ADR-006 for manual drop-JD while unblocking queue-mirrored fan-out. Tailor owns the feature-branch commit+push and gh pr create.
implications: Manual resume-tailor runs unchanged: user creates the branch before job-description.md.
Queue-invoked runs: tailor creates the branch, writes P2-J1 job-description.md, then Steps 1-5.
Orchestrator does not merge feature branches to main.
P2-G6s after a merged PR: recreate the feature branch from current main, overwrite the sandbox, open a new PR; the user merges over files already on main.

ADR-045 supersedes queue-invoked slug derivation only. Mint writes company_slug and position_slug (always-suffix from source_job_id). Tailor honors those fields and does not re-kebab title. Manual drop-JD still uses unsuffixed parent folders (ADR-006 / ADR-011). First-ship queue-invoked identity kebab_case(company)+kebab_case(title) remains true for historical unsuffixed winner PRs.

alternatives_considered.option: Orchestrator bypasses the PR gate
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Human PR review/merge remains the hard gate.

alternatives_considered.option: Slug derivation from JD free text
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Branch identity is kebab_case listing company and title (ADR-011).

alternatives_considered.option: Orchestrator-prepared workspace, sandbox manifest, or split git Step 5 (Options A/B/C)
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Handoff is queue-mirrored with tailor-owned feature-branch git.

decisions.title: Locked Agent Policies File (Rename and Multi-Agent Envelope)
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Phase 2 needs execution policy for more than job-analysis. A single-object locked-job-analysis-policy.json cannot hold per-agent configs without splitting SoT or rewriting ADR-026.
drivers: One human-maintained locked file for all agent execution/cost knobs.
Preserve git history via git mv.
Shared execution keys; extra objects per record (research, parallel) as data-model extensions.
ADR-026 remains the 1b sequential-analysis cost decision; this ADR extends it.

decision_outcome.selected_option: git mv locked-job-analysis-policy.json to locked-agent-policies.json. Envelope schema_version plus policies[]. Keep job_analysis_policy_001 (execution, research, P2-P1 parallel). Add resume_tailor_policy_001 (execution only). New agents add a policies[] record, not a new locked JSON file. job-orchestrator has no first-ship record.
decision_outcome.justification: Envelope plus id lookup scales to every agent without forking policy files or mutating ADR-026 history. Identical execution keys keep batch grain comparable. Analysis-only extensions keep tailor fan-out serial.
implications: Consumers look up by policy id, not by filename-as-singleton.
CI and validate_guardrails_json.py retarget the new path.
Agents never edit the file.

alternatives_considered.option: Second locked JSON for resume-tailor
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Splits execution-policy SoT and duplicates envelope/validation.

alternatives_considered.option: Rewrite ADR-026 selected_option to the new filename
alternatives_considered.reasoning: ADRs append; they do not rewrite history.

alternatives_considered.option: Copy then delete the old file
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Execution constraints require move to preserve git history.

decisions.title: Ban Instance and Locked-File Schema Versioning (Git + ADRs Are History)
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Instance envelopes and two locked JSON files carried schema_version or version keys that consumers already ignored. Git history and appended ADRs already record shape changes. Keeping those keys implied a compatibility shim and forced writers, validators, and live files to stay in lockstep with unused numbers.
drivers: Drop every versioning key in the current tree: instance schema_version, locked-agent-policies envelope schema_version, per-policy version, criteria version.
Keep criteria created_on / modified_on. No broader envelope-field audit this pass.
Ship schema, writers, validators, tests, live main files, and this ADR in one change. additionalProperties: false makes a split ship fail CI.
No git history rewrite. Fail-closed on leftover versioning keys.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Remove schema_version from job-search instance envelopes and from locked-agent-policies.json. Remove version from each policies[] record and from locked-job-search-criteria.json. Shape changes are recorded by appending ADRs and git history. Validators fail-closed on leftover versioning keys.
decision_outcome.justification: Policy lookup is by id. The dashboard does not read versioning keys. Git plus ADRs are the history. Leftover keys must fail closed the same way leftover mode and pull_date already do on queues.
implications: PULL_FILE, APPROVED_JOBS, and ANALYSIS_FILE no longer list schema_version; additionalProperties: false rejects the key.
Analysis-request and tailor-request validators forbid schema_version.
Writers stop emitting the keys. Live dated jobs.json, analyses, and approved-jobs.json on main are stripped in place.
Do not rewrite ADR-012, ADR-023, ADR-026, or ADR-029. Shipped 1b and Phase 2 child plans stay historical SoT.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep envelope versions as a compatibility shim
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Consumers already ignore the keys. A shim preserves unused numbers without a reader.

alternatives_considered.option: Rewrite older ADRs in place
alternatives_considered.reasoning: ADRs append; they do not rewrite history.

alternatives_considered.option: History rewrite / git filter-repo
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Same as ADR-027: strip the current tree only.

decisions.title: Orchestrator History Sandbox for Run Log
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: The job-orchestrator needs a durable last-run log for the local dashboard. Cursor cannot dump IDE chat. Job-search and resume-tailor sandboxes are owned by other agents; putting orch operational files there mixes ownership. Core-architecture forbids new directories outside the locked tree without an explicit ADR.
drivers: Give the orchestrator its own history sandbox, parallel to job-search and resume-tailor.
Skill dual-write only: whatever the orchestrator would put in chat is also appended to disk. No IDE transcript dump. No nested analysis/tailor chat files.
Keep P2-D1 dashboard serve root at .ai/history/job-search/ so the URL stays /dashboard/.
Ship this ADR in the same change as the directory, core-architecture line, gitignore, and dashboard log panel.

decision_outcome.selected_option: New sandbox .ai/history/orchestrator/ with tracked .gitkeep and gitignored run.log (stable name). Truncate at orchestrator run start (P2-D1 adjacent); persist at run end. UTF-8 append-only lines prefixed with UTC ISO timestamps. Dashboard maps HTTP /orchestrator/run.log onto that file without changing the serve root.
decision_outcome.justification: A dedicated sandbox keeps orchestrator operational state out of job-search and resume-tailor trees. A stable gitignored run.log is the disk SoT for the dashboard panel. Dual-write from the skill is the only feasible chat capture. Changing the serve root would move the locked P2-D1 dashboard URL.
implications: Agents and operators treat .ai/history/orchestrator/ as the job-orchestrator sandbox. run.log is not committed.
orch_run_log.py truncates and appends that path. The dashboard poll/Refresh replaces the panel from the full file. Missing file is an empty/muted placeholder.
serve.py keeps the HTTP root at .ai/history/job-search/ and serves the sibling log at /orchestrator/run.log.
Do not rewrite ADR-003 or ADR-011. Nested analysis/tailor transcripts and IDE dump stay out of scope.

alternatives_considered.option: Store run.log under .ai/history/job-search/dashboard/
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Job-search owns that sandbox. Orchestrator operational files would mix agent ownership and directory purpose.

alternatives_considered.option: Store run.log under .ai/history/resume-tailor/
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Resume-tailor sandboxes are per company/position (ADR-011) and must not hold orchestrator run state.

alternatives_considered.option: Change P2-D1 serve root to .ai/history/ so both trees are children
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Would move the dashboard URL off /dashboard/ and reopen the locked serve-root contract.

alternatives_considered.option: Literal Cursor IDE transcript dump or nested analysis/tailor chat files
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Cursor cannot dump IDE chat. Subagent transcripts appear only if the orchestrator copies them into its own chat/log.

decisions.title: Rebuild Skips Post-Handoff Ledger Rows and Sidecars
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: G10 locked --rebuild as pre-handoff only: wipe today's sidecars and matching approved-jobs.json rows. After Phase 2, write_analysis_stubs.py --rebuild still dropped in_progress|failed|completed|deployed rows. A 2026-08-31 GHA rebuild deleted the completed E2E ledger row for greenhouse:lts:4372981009 and stubbed its sidecar. Consume already refuses to mutate POST_HANDOFF_STATUSES.
drivers: Keep G10 wipe for pre-handoff approved rows and jobs with no ledger row.
Pair sidecar and ledger: skipping only the ledger drop leaves a completed row pointing at a revision-0 stub.
Do not implement the Option C rebuild-manifest cascade (P2-R1) in this change.
Do not rewrite ADR-023 or the historical 1b G10 child-plan body.

decision_outcome.selected_option: On --rebuild, skip sidecar unlink, skip ledger drop, and skip writing a new stub when the matching approved-jobs.json row status is in_progress, failed, completed, or deployed. approved rows and jobs with no ledger row still wipe. jobs.json rebuild still resets presence to new.
decision_outcome.justification: Post-handoff execution state is durable. Consume already treats those statuses as immutable. Wiping the sidecar without the ledger (or the reverse) desyncs G4 FKs. Full Option C cleanup remains parked as P2-R1.
implications: write_analysis_stubs.py imports POST_HANDOFF_STATUSES from consume_analysis_queue.py.
A missing sidecar for a post-handoff ledger row stays missing; rebuild does not invent a stub.
GHA --rebuild remains source-scoped. Orchestrator does not consume rebuild-manifest.json.
Do not rewrite ADR-023. 1b G10 historical text stays. P2-R1 stays parked.

alternatives_considered.option: Skip ledger drop only; still delete+recreate those sidecars
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Produces a completed or failed ledger row pointing at a revision-0 stub. The next orch run re-queues the stub; consume still will not retarget the ledger.

alternatives_considered.option: Also keep approved rows and their sidecars
alternatives_considered.reasoning: approved is pre-handoff. G10 wipe of those rows remains the way to force a fresh first-fill after rebuild.

alternatives_considered.option: Ship the full Option C rebuild-manifest cascade in this change
alternatives_considered.reasoning: P2-R1 stays parked. This ADR only stops rebuild from destroying post-handoff state.

decisions.title: Analysis-Row Telemetry, Queue Invoke, and Orchestrator Run-Log Trailer
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: Filled analysis sidecars and the orchestrator run.log had no closed place to store token/context usage. Phase 1b parked telemetry as a future analysis_runs[] entity and stored queue run_id only. Ledger session remains a separate parked grill. additionalProperties: false means new sidecar keys must ship with live backfill in the same change.
drivers: Telemetry is keys on the filled analyses[] row, not a new analysis_runs[] entity. Queue run_id copy onto the row is unchanged.
Queue envelope invoke is manual|batch, not mode (still forbidden). Generator --invoke optional, default batch, independent of --job-id. Orchestrator never passes --invoke.
Batch/nested analysis writes every usage key as JSON null; context_metric_status is not_programmatically_available. Do not invent tokens or %.
Orchestrator run.log needs a replaceable trailer using the same closed keys, rewritten each orch turn for this orch session only. Dashboard log widget pins that trailer as a footer. Disk is SoT.
Ship schema, writers, validators, tests, 17 live sidecars, dashboard, skills, and this ADR in one change.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Required null-ok telemetry keys on every analyses[] row (including stubs): started_at, ended_at, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_tokens_in, thinking_tokens, context_usage_percent; context_metric_status is not_programmatically_available|observed. Queue envelope required invoke manual|batch. orch_run_log.py --telemetry replaces a delimiter-plus-JSON trailer; --append preserves it. Dashboard Current analysis shows a Run accordion; #log-panel is a 240px column with scrolling #log-viewport and pinned #log-telemetry footer.
decision_outcome.justification: Row keys avoid a new analysis_runs[] entity and keep queue run_id as the batch join. invoke is not mode. Nested agents cannot observe parent tokens, so batch writes nulls. A trailer on the existing gitignored run.log is the SoT without a second telemetry file. The log footer must not scroll away with chat lines.
implications: locked-job-search-data-model.json $defs/analysis requires the closed keys. additionalProperties: false rejects a split ship.
generate-analysis-queue.py --invoke default batch. validate_analysis_request requires invoke and still forbids mode.
write_analysis_stubs.py stub_document emits nulls plus not_programmatically_available. Live sidecars are null-backfilled in this change.
job-analysis reads envelope invoke only. job-orchestrator never passes --invoke and rewrites the trailer each orch turn. Do not sum nested analysis/tailor usage into the orch trailer.
Do not rewrite ADR-023, ADR-030, ADR-031, or ADR-032. Ledger session stays parked. Do not rewrite 1b G10 historical analysis_runs[] text.

alternatives_considered.option: New analysis_runs[] entity keyed by ledger run_id
alternatives_considered.reasoning: P2-A1 is row telemetry. Queue run_id copy is already the batch join. A new entity would reopen 1b G10 parking without adding a reader.

alternatives_considered.option: Reuse envelope mode for manual vs batch
alternatives_considered.reasoning: mode is forbidden leftover. invoke is a new required enum.

alternatives_considered.option: Second gitignored telemetry file next to run.log
alternatives_considered.reasoning: The trailer on run.log is the disk SoT. A sibling file splits the dashboard poll.

alternatives_considered.option: Sum nested analysis/tailor token usage into the orch trailer
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Nested agents write nulls. The trailer is this orch session only.

decisions.title: Deploy Tailored Outreach with Resume-Tailor Artifacts
decisions.author: IT Solution Architect

context.problem_statement: ADR-006 deploys the tailored resume, application DOCX, and engineering log to each Google Drive role folder while tailored-outreach.md remains repository-only. The outreach message is an operational application asset and must be available beside the deployed resume artifacts.
drivers: Deploy the complete set of candidate-facing application assets to the existing company/role folder.
Preserve changed-sandbox deployment scope and avoid backfilling unrelated historical sandboxes.
Use deterministic Drive names so repeated deployments update the existing outreach file.
Keep job-description.md repository-only because it is source/audit material rather than a candidate-facing artifact.

decision_outcome.selected_option: Stage tailored-outreach.md in dist/resume-tailor, record it as outreach_artifact in resume-tailor-manifest.json, and upsert it to the existing Google Drive company/role folder as tailored-outreach.md.
decision_outcome.justification: The manifest builder already requires tailored-outreach.md for every changed resume-tailor sandbox, and the Drive synchronizer already handles deterministic per-role upserts. Extending those existing paths adds the artifact without changing workflow orchestration, folder structure, credentials, or deployment triggers.
implications: build_resume_tailor_manifest.py fails when tailored-outreach.md is missing and stages it with the other deploy artifacts.
sync_gdrive.py uploads tailored-outreach.md beside tailored-resume.md, engineering-log.md, and the application DOCX.
cd-main.yml requires no structural change because it already transfers the complete dist directory between build and deploy jobs.
Historical ADR-006 text and deployed plans are not rewritten; this decision supersedes only their repository-only treatment of tailored-outreach.md.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep tailored-outreach.md in git only
alternatives_considered.reasoning: The outreach message would remain separated from the deployed assets used to execute the application.

alternatives_considered.option: Deploy every audit artifact, including job-description.md
alternatives_considered.reasoning: The job description remains source/audit material and is not required in the candidate-facing Drive folder.

alternatives_considered.option: Add a separate outreach deployment workflow
